about.title: Yorba Linda Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Yorba Linda's collisions tend to track its busiest corridors: commuters funneling onto Imperial Highway, everyday local traffic along Yorba Linda Boulevard, and steady flow on Bastanchury Road and La Palma Avenue. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, the city logged 91 injury collisions that left 116 people hurt, with no traffic deaths recorded. Reports cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when the commute home overlaps with weekend errands. If one of those collisions involved you, the days that follow can feel disorganized. Medical bills arrive before the insurer calls back, the other driver's story may shift, and you are asked to make decisions while still sore. LawProactive exists to simplify one part of that. We are not a law firm. We connect you, at no cost, with an independent Orange County personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency. You pay nothing to be matched, and the attorney only earns a fee if your case produces a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Yorba Linda Drivers Use LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than Most People Expect
items.desc: California generally allows two years to file a car accident injury claim, but that window can shrink to six months when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting an attorney in place early keeps those dates from sneaking up on you.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you shared some blame for the crash; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages in car accident cases, so pain, disruption, and lost enjoyment of life all count. The attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Imperial Highway on a Friday evening. What should I do before talking to the other driver's insurer?
items.answer: Start by getting checked out medically, even if you feel mostly fine, because soft-tissue and head injuries often surface a day or two later. Photograph your vehicle, the roadway, and any visible injuries, and save the police report number and witness contacts. Politely decline to give the other insurer a recorded statement until you have spoken with an attorney; those recordings are often used to minimize what you are owed.

items.question: The other driver says I was partly at fault. Can I still make a claim in California?
items.answer: Yes. California follows pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible reduces your recovery rather than eliminating it. If you were found 20 percent at fault, for example, you could still pursue 80 percent of your damages. An attorney can review the evidence and challenge any fault percentage the insurer assigns unfairly.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm, and what does it cost to use?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match Yorba Linda residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident cases in Orange County. There is no charge to be connected, and the attorney works on contingency, so you owe no legal fee unless your case results in a recovery.
